subject: Tenant SLA & throughput mapping — isolation and capacity workshop
messages:
From: Adrian Kim <adrian.kim@brightline.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment throughput baseline + isolation requirements

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on — we want to make sure the private deployment (VPC) for Brightline is sized correctly and that tenant isolation meets our SLA needs. High-level asks: 

- Target steady-state throughput: 200 req/s for chat (avg response: ~400 tokens), 1200 embeddings req/s (single-vector).
- Peak/day: up to 4x sustained for 30-90 minutes (so plan for headroom and graceful degradation).
- Isolation: per-tenant admission control and soft QoS so one tenant doesn't steal KV cache or saturate egress.
- Models: we will run two variants — a quantized 33B model for chat and a 7B optimized for embeddings; both loaded per-tenant.
- Network constraints: our datacenter limits outbound NAT to a single egress IP with 8Gbps peak; we'd prefer per-tenant NAT or NAT pools.

Can your team propose a starting capacity configuration and a short list of failure modes (network egress exhaustion, cold cache storms, model-loading thundering herd) with recommended mitigations? We can share model profiles.

Attaching a brief model profile (brightline_model_profile.json) and we can set up a 60-minute sizing workshop this week.

Best,
Adrian
Adrian Kim
Head of Infrastructure, Brightline AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 19:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput baseline + isolation requirements

Adrian — thanks for the clear summary. Initial thoughts below, and we attached a working sizing workbook (private_capacity_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the detailed math.

Short answer (starter config):
- 4 nodes × A100 80GB (single-tenant pool) per tenant class for chat (estimate ~180–220 req/s sustained per 4-GPU pool for quantized-33B with Redwood runtime, concurrency=8, batching tuned).
- 2 nodes × A100 40GB (or 4×40GB) for embeddings per tenant class (we expect ~300–500 embeddings/sec per 2×A100 depending on batch sizing and fp16/INT8 path).
- Admission control: token-based admission + dynamic concurrency cap per-tenant.
- Cache warmup: we recommend pre-loading hot KV for top 10 tenants and a staggered warm-start schedule.

Failure modes & mitigations (short list):
- Egress saturation: use NAT pools + per-tenant egress policing; fall back to queued SDK responses with a 503+Retry header for non-critical traffic.
- Cold-start spikes: prioritize model prefetch for flagged tenants, add short-lived burst pool for fast model-loading.
- Model eviction contention: implement per-tenant pinned model slots and an eviction-cost heuristic in the cache manager.

Questions for the workshop:
1) Do you require strict hardware isolation (dedicated GPUs) per tenant or logical isolation with QoS?
2) Can you provide realistic peak request traces (one-week sample) and the percent of long-running vs short completions?

We propose a 60-minute workshop Wednesday 11/4 at 16:00 UTC to run through the workbook and network diagram.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput baseline + isolation requirements — sizing workbook notes

Hi team — I pulled together the initial assumptions and a conservative/probabilistic sizing model in the workbook. Key assumptions (summary):

- Quantized 33B chat: avg tokens/generated = 400, avg tokens/req = 450 (includes prompt).
- Per-GPU throughput (empirical): 45–60 chat req/s (per A100-80 with batching window=60ms, concurrency 8).
- Embeddings model (7B optimized): ~250 vec/s per A100-40 at batch size 512; latency SLA 75ms p95 for single-vector requests.
- Headroom target: 2.5x on sustained baseline, 4x for short peaks up to 90 minutes.

Mapping example for Tenant A (baseline needs):
- Chat baseline 75 req/s -> allocate 2×A100-80 equivalent (gives ~100–120 rps with headroom to 250 rps).
- Embeddings baseline 400 req/s -> allocate 2×A100-40 (gives ~500–600 rps with headroom).

I've added a short sheet with sensitivity sweeps (change batching, concurrency) and a column with cost estimates for dedicated vs shared pools. Please review before the workshop.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Adrian Kim <adrian.kim@brightline.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput baseline + isolation requirements — network and ops considerations

Adrian / team — adding the network and ops constraints we need to plan for on the VPC/on-prem side. Attaching a reference topology (vpc_network_diagram.pdf).

Network/ops checklist (high level):
- Egress: single NAT IP + 8Gbps cap is a hard constraint. Options: NAT pools (per-tenant set) or egress-gateway appliances. If NAT pools not possible, plan strict per-tenant egress shaping at the boundary.
- Model artifact store: prefer a local model cache replicated over 10GbE; initial cold loads will hit object storage (S3 or S3-compatible) — plan for parallel fetch throttles to avoid saturating ingress.
- Storage: checkpoint and KV storage should be on NVMe-backed volumes; network filesystem levels used only for cold model artifacts.
- Observability hooks: token-level telemetry + admission control counters, per-tenant cache hit-rate dashboards, and export to your Prometheus/Grafana.
- Failure injection: run a short test to simulate a cold-cache storm (8 simultaneous tenants reload) and confirm graceful degradation policy.

Throughput-to-network mapping (back-of-envelope):
- 1 chat req (avg 450 tokens) outbound egress to model repo + logs ~= 4–6KB; embeddings vector ~2KB per req. These are small; biggest impact is parallel artifact pulls and telemetry bursts.

Recommendation: plan a 10GbE uplink for the pool host VLAN and a small egress gateway with per-tenant shaping. We'll bring a simple iptables tc profile to the workshop.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

- NAT pools: we can request a second egress IP range from our colo but it takes ~2 weeks; for now we'll accept per-tenant shaping.
